canonical_id: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit activation-adherence decomposition

source.paper: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
source.venue_note: Official release README labels the paper EMNLP 2026 Main

artifact_evidence.paper_drivers: examples/harness-evolution/ includes separate Exp0 evolver-side and Exp1 solver-side drivers plus single-seed sweep launchers, model/region mapping and HFR diagnostic pipeline.
artifact_evidence.benchmark_adapters: Official release includes SWE-bench Verified, MCP-Atlas and SkillsBench agents/adapters, seed workspaces, evolution engine and harness contract.
artifact_evidence.isolation_design: README specifies Exp0 fixes the solver/agent while varying the evolver to isolate harness-updating; Exp1 fixes the evolver while varying the solver to isolate harness-benefit. A train/test split route is additionally exposed for held-out benefit estimation.
artifact_evidence.activation_adherence_diagnostic: HFR pipeline extracts per-skill rubrics, judges trajectory adherence and computes retrieval-to-use gap, early termination and answer-before-validation proxies.
artifact_evidence.upstream_pinning: SkillsBench auto-clone is documented as pinned to commit 828bb921... and a vendored/source-pin surface exists for official Terminus integration.

environment.dependency_policy: minimum-version ranges rather than a fully hashed environment lock

artifact_evidence.result_surface: Experiment commands write output directories/results during execution, but a committed complete paper-results matrix was not identified in the audited branch tree.

paper_claims.updating_flatness: The paper reports small spread in useful harness-update gains across evolvers of very different base capability; the clean worker records best-vs-worst spread no more than 3.1 pp on any benchmark under the tested protocol.
paper_claims.small_evolver_result: The clean worker records Qwen3.5-9B as best on SkillsBench in the paper's harness-updating metric (+3.8 pp), versus Opus 4.6 +2.3 and Qwen3-235B +1.5; retain as primary-paper cells pending independent rerun.
paper_claims.benefit_nonmonotonicity: The paper reports weak-tier agents benefit little, mid-tier agents most, and strong-tier agents less than mid-tier under the tested harness-benefit protocol.
paper_claims.activation_failure: The clean worker records an approximately 25% harness-load rate for Qwen3-32B versus approximately 96% for strong models; exact cells should remain paper-scoped until independently reproduced.

reproducibility_assessment.official_artifact_support: strong for experimental decomposition, benchmark runners, seed harnesses and activation/adherence diagnostics
reproducibility_assessment.independent_replication: not identified in targeted public search on 2026-08-25
reproducibility_assessment.judgment: The official release makes the central conceptual separation executable: the evolver and solver factors are independently varied by dedicated experiment drivers, and the HFR diagnostic exposes the retrieval/activation/adherence path that supports the paper's interpretation. This is stronger than a paper-only claim. However, the release does not by itself independently validate the reported cross-model numerical cells; benchmark services, hosted models and environment versions remain external, and no third-party full rerun was located.
exact_blockers: No independently reproduced Exp0/Exp1 matrix or HFR table was found in the targeted public search.
The audited branch uses dependency lower bounds rather than a hashed lockfile, so future dependency drift can affect exact replay.

SWE-bench execution depends on Docker images/datasets, MCP-Atlas depends on containerized MCP servers, per-server credentials and an LLM judge, and SkillsBench is fetched from an upstream pinned repository; these are nontrivial external runtime dependencies.
The studied models are accessed through hosted Bedrock/OpenAI-compatible backends; provider/model behavior can drift from the original paper execution.
A complete committed original-paper result/output matrix was not identified in the audited branch tree; reproducing paper cells requires rerunning the expensive sweeps.
Harness-Following Rate includes judge-based adherence assessment in addition to mechanical proxies, so exact historical HFR values depend on judge behavior/configuration.
reproducibility_assessment.scope: Strong evidence that the claimed updating-vs-benefit decomposition and activation/adherence diagnostic are implemented and can be rerun. Do not treat flat evolver scaling or non-monotonic solver benefit as universal laws; they remain bounded to the tested models, three benchmarks, seed harnesses and fixed evolution protocol.

downstream_note: This artifact is directly useful for evaluating whether a persistent improvement fails because the artifact is poor versus because the executor never retrieves/activates/follows it. Preserve those stages separately in downstream evaluation instead of scoring only end-task outcome.
